questions.q: What is the single purpose of the digital boundary?
options: To prove your willpower
To protect your attention for God during the time you have set aside
To reject technology
To impress your support person
questions.explanation: It is not a test, a fast to be proud of, or a boundary against help. If you slip and check something, you have noticed, and you can put it down again.

questions.q: Why does the chapter say 'airplane mode with an emergency channel' is not an arrangement at all?
options: Because airplane mode drains the battery
Because a phone in airplane mode cannot ordinarily receive a call
Because emergencies never happen on retreat
Because airplane mode is forbidden
questions.explanation: You must choose one of two fundamentally different arrangements: stay reachable for emergencies with Focus/Do Not Disturb, or disconnect completely with scheduled checks.

questions.q: Which arrangement does the chapter recommend for parents, caregivers, and anyone with safety needs?
options: Airplane mode with scheduled checks
Focus or Do Not Disturb with selected emergency contacts allowed through
Leaving the phone at home
A phone held by retreat staff
questions.explanation: Cellular service stays on, everything is silenced except one or two designated contacts, and the arrangement is tested before you leave, not on Day 1.

questions.q: What does the chapter ask you to do with your emergency contact before the retreat?
options: Give them your social media passwords
Define together what counts as a genuine emergency, say it out loud, and agree what they do if you don't answer
Ask them to message you each morning
Nothing, they will know when to call
questions.explanation: A genuine emergency does not include ordinary questions or routine work decisions. Ask them to call rather than message so there is no ambiguity.

options: Not owning a Bible
Opening a Bible app places Scripture beside the apps that compete for your attention; bring a printed Bible if you can
Bible apps do not work offline
Reading too many translations
questions.explanation: If a phone is your only option, disable notifications, be honest about how Day 1 goes, and switch to paper on Day 2 if it is not working.

questions.q: What does the chapter say about worship music and podcasts during the retreat?
options: Use them constantly to stay focused
Music is allowed in a limited way, but the default is silence; leave podcasts, sermons and audiobooks aside unless a session directs you to one
Only instrumental music is permitted
All sound is forbidden
questions.explanation: The programme already provides structured input. Do not use music to fill every quiet moment; if silence triggers severe distress, follow Chapter 5's guidance.

reflection: What is your honest reaction to the thought of three days without your phone? Write it down without judging it.
Which arrangement are you choosing, who is your emergency contact, and when will you test it?
How will you read Scripture and this guide during the retreat? If the answer is "on my phone," what will you do to make that workable?
Fill in the written agreement from the chapter.
